title: Google: drug-equivalence and disease claims for unapproved products
rule_summary: Google doesn't allow ads for products that imply they're as effective as prescription drugs or controlled substances, non-government-approved products implying they're safe or effective for a disease, supplements with active pharmaceutical or dangerous ingredients, products subject to government action or warning, or names confusingly similar to unapproved substances.
source_title: Google Ads policy: Healthcare and medicines
citation: Google Ads policy: Healthcare and medicines > Unapproved substances
compliant_examples: Creatine monohydrate, 5 g per serving, third-party tested.

title: Google: prescription drug names in ads, keywords and landing pages
rule_summary: Google restricts prescription drug terms in ads, landing pages and keywords. Supplement copy that names a prescription drug (for example 'a natural Ozempic alternative') risks disapproval as well as an FDA drug-comparison issue.
source_title: Google Ads policy: Healthcare and medicines
citation: Google Ads policy: Healthcare and medicines > Restricted drug terms
